tweets.text:
Ben Thompson on why Google and Amazon are Nvidia's biggest competitors, and what they're doing about it:

"Google and Amazon aren't selling their chips on differentiation. They're selling chips as commodities. Nvidia's the one selling the differentiation.

So that's Nvidia's biggest problem, because what's the number one advantage that the hyperscalers have?

Lower cost of capital. It's a capital fight. They have a lower cost of capital than the neoclouds do.

Intel is a good example here. AMD cleaned them out in hyperscaler sales, because the hyperscalers put in the effort to get stuff working on AMD versus Intel. Because they're buying at such scale, the investment to do that is worth it.

The part of Intel's business that never floundered was selling to government and selling to enterprises, because they don't have the resources of a hyperscaler. 

That's why Nvidia talks about selling to sovereign clouds, that's why they talk about selling to enterprises. 

They want to get into markets where they're not going to be balancing this chip versus that chip.

The hyperscalers have always been the threat to Nvidia for that reason, because they're actually bigger."

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — AUGUST 21 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

The Treasury’s decision to double buybacks of long-dated bonds weakened the dollar and intensified concerns over fiscal stress and financial repression. Gold has also broken decisively above its 200-day moving average.

The message across all four metals: capital is moving toward scarce real assets just as security of future supply becomes increasingly valuable.

#uranium #niobium $RSH.CN $M.CN $MYRUF

THE RUSH ARBITRAGE — MYRIAD AT A DISCOUNT, BOXI FOR FREE

At ~C$0.23, each Rush share will receive 0.5405 Myriad shares. Even using Myriad’s previous C$0.45 close, those shares alone are worth approximately C$0.243 per Rush share—already more than the Rush purchase price.

On top of that, Rush holders receive one SpinCo share for every four Rush shares. SpinCo will own Boxi and start with C$100,000 in cash.

The market is therefore assigning Boxi virtually zero value.

Yet the Boxi samples are spectacular:

• Up to 26.92% Nb₂O₅
• The ten highest niobium samples range from 1.01% to 26.92% Nb₂O₅
• Uranium samples reached 11.90% U₃O₈—that’s 119,000 ppm
• Even the tenth-highest uranium sample shown returned 0.24% U₃O₈, or 2,400 ppm

Niobium is a critical metal used to make steel stronger and lighter and in aerospace applications. Supply is highly concentrated, while the U.S. remains completely import-dependent. For perspective, NioCorp’s advanced Elk Creek project reports a 0.79% Nb₂O₅ reserve grade.

That is not a like-for-like comparison: Boxi’s figures are selected surface samples, not deposit-wide grades. They show that exceptionally high-grade material exists—but they do not yet establish width, continuity, tonnage, recoveries or an economic resource.

Boxi now needs systematic geophysics, drilling and metallurgical work.

That is the asymmetry: Rush investors are effectively paying only for the Myriad shares while receiving a potentially significant niobium-uranium exploration asset for free.

Disclosure: I own Rush shares, and Myriad Uranium is a commercial partner.

On top of that, Rush holders receive one SpinCo share for every four Rush shares. SpinCo will own Boxi and start with C$100,000 in cash.

The market is therefore assigning Boxi virtually zero value.

Yet the Boxi samples are spectacular:

• Up to 26.92% Nb₂O₅
• The ten highest niobium samples range from 1.01% to 26.92% Nb₂O₅
• Uranium samples reached 11.90% U₃O₈—that’s 119,000 ppm
• Even the tenth-highest uranium sample shown returned 0.24% U₃O₈, or 2,400 ppm

Niobium is a critical metal used to make steel stronger and lighter and in aerospace applications. Supply is highly concentrated, while the U.S. remains completely import-dependent. For perspective, NioCorp’s advanced Elk Creek project reports a 0.79% Nb₂O₅ reserve grade.

That is not a like-for-like comparison: Boxi’s figures are selected surface samples, not deposit-wide grades. They show that exceptionally high-grade material exists—but they do not yet establish width, continuity, tonnage, recoveries or an economic resource.

Boxi now needs systematic geophysics, drilling and metallurgical work.

That is the asymmetry: Rush investors are effectively paying only for the Myriad shares while receiving a potentially significant niobium-uranium exploration asset for free.

Disclosure: I own Rush shares, and Myriad Uranium is a commercial partner.

tweets.text:
Real connection lives in inconvenience.

A few months ago I sat down with @PeterDiamandis  and @salimismail on The Journeyman and we got into this. 

Salim made a brilliant point... in the nineties we introduced video calls so nobody would ever have to travel again. Yet the conference industry has never been bigger. We still get on the plane, sit in traffic and stand around hotel lobbies. Why? because community is worth the inconvenience. Putting yourself out for other people is exactly what makes it mean something.

We've spent decades optimising for a hyper-convenient life. And the machines will finish the job... they'll be able to do everything convenient. The one thing they can't do is show up. Be in the room. Be there.

That's why Im not worried about whats coming. The things that make us human are about to become the most valuable things we have.
